clue.text: Southern border plant

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south or southern
a border is an edge

explanation.surface: A plant growing along a garden border in the south.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a grass-like marsh plant, a common example of waterside vegetation.

clue.text: Phil cares about being like a ball

indicators.note: about can mean around, here moving the letters of Phil cares into a new order

explanation.surface: Phil worries about putting on weight and becoming round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a sphere, so anything shaped like one is round in that geometric sense.

clue.text: Student withdrawing to re-start at Rugby

definitions.meaning: someone who leaves a course before finishing it
in rugby union, a drop kick from the 22-metre line used to restart play

explanation.surface: A student pulls out of college to start again at Rugby School.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby is both a famous English public school and the game named after it; the surface reads the school, the definition needs the game.
explanation.definitionFit: A college quitter is called this informally, and the same term names a rugby drop kick restarting play.

clue.text: Girl who is all energy when retired

indicators.note: when retired says the hidden letters are read backwards
is here means contains: the phrase all energy holds the letters within it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A girl so lively she seems pure energy, even in retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Girl who' as the definition, but 'who' cannot stand in for a name; 'Girl' alone defines, and 'who is' leads into the hidden run.
explanation.definitionFit: A short feminine first name, as borne by the singer Fitzgerald.

clue.text: 18 disturbing men's orbit

indicators.note: disturbing suggests throwing things into disorder, so the letters of men's orbit are rearranged

parts.note: the apostrophe adds no letter; the fodder is MENSORBIT

explanation.surface: Something unsettles the circuit followed by a group of men.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' points to the answer of 18 down, BUTTERFLY: this is a yellow species of it. The word is also an old name for sulphur.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a sulphur-yellow species of the winged insect at 18.

clue.text: If silent, a mini can be barely noticeable

indicators.note: can be signals that these letters may become something else when reorganised

explanation.surface: A Mini car running silently can hardly be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something infinitely small is so tiny that one can scarcely detect it.

clue.text: Flag over a chronicle

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece above the second

parts.note: to flag is to droop or tire, to sag

explanation.surface: A flag flies above a historical record.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrative history, especially a Norse tale, is a chronicle of events.

clue.text: Individual turning sour is oppressive

parts.note: an individual is one person

indicators.note: turning suggests the letters of sour are spun round into a new order

explanation.surface: A person turning sour makes life a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome task weighs heavily on someone, which is what oppressive means.

clue.text: Small arch

definitions.meaning: small and delicate, like a fairy
as an adjective, arch means playfully mischievous

explanation.walkthrough: 'arch' looks like a noun, a curved structure, but here it is the adjective meaning roguish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairy-like describes things both dainty in size and impishly mischievous, matching each sense.

clue.text: Clyde, for example, puts cowl on chimney

indicators.note: puts on places the first piece ahead of the second in this across entry
puts on places the first piece ahead of the second in this across entry

parts.note: a cowl is a hood
lum is a Scottish and northern word for a chimney

explanation.surface: Someone fits a cowl on top of a chimney.
explanation.walkthrough: Clyde is Clyde Barrow of Bonnie and Clyde, the American gangster, not the Scottish river; the river sense is reinforced by the Scots LUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Clyde Barrow was a gangster, and a hood or thug is an example of a criminal of that kind.

clue.text: Unsociable sort, yet makes imprint as host

indicators.note: makes says the letters of imprint as host form something new

explanation.surface: A grumpy loner nonetheless leaves a mark as host.
explanation.definitionFit: A hater of humankind avoids company, so is an unsociable person.

clue.text: Cover deployed for opening pair

parts.note: the first couple of Genesis, Adam and Eve, covered their nakedness with leaves; the opening pair also hints at cricket openers

explanation.surface: Fielding cover is set for the two opening batsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket vocabulary (cover is a fielding position, openers bat first) misleads; the opening pair are Adam and Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam and Eve sewed leaves of this tree to hide themselves, making a covering for modesty.

clue.text: High position of showy violinist

parts.note: refers to the musical Fiddler on the ..., whose title fiddler plays atop a house

explanation.surface: A flamboyant violinist reaches the top of the profession.
explanation.definitionFit: The fiddler in the famous musical is perched up on top of a house, so this is his lofty spot.

clue.text: Turning to account, causing accountant to leave

indicators.note: to leave says the accountant's letters are taken out of causing

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant

explanation.surface: A firm turns to the books, making its accountant quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn something to account is to make use of it, employing it.

clue.text: Blue county?

definitions.meaning: feeling blue is feeling low, depressed
County ... is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Being low in spirits is being sad, and it is also the name of a Northern Ireland county.

clue.text: Bulb lit has a bit charge

parts.note: a light that is lit is switched on
an ion is a particle carrying a small electric charge

explanation.surface: A light bulb that is lit carries some electrical charge.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable grows as a bulb, an example of an edible one.

clue.text: Indian ruler, the last character in principle revolution

indicators.note: in places the last letter within the reversed word
revolution suggests turning round, so the word for principal is read backwards

parts.note: used here for principal, meaning main; the spelling is the setter's slip for the homophone
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian prince personifies the ultimate in revolutionary principle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'principle' should be 'principal' (main); read backwards that is NIAM, and Z goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the title of the ruler of Hyderabad, an Indian princely state.

clue.text: Stormy Atlantic is one location of this old scourge

indicators.note: a stormy sea is tossed about, so the letters of Atlantic is one are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: The wild Atlantic was where sailors once faced this flogging whip.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly an &lit: the whip was used to flog sailors at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: This was a knotted whip with several cords, an old instrument of naval punishment.

clue.text: Orange-tip, for example, as orange-blossom on stage

definitions.meaning: the orange-tip is a British species of winged insect
the bride of Puccini's opera Madama ... wears bridal orange blossom on stage

explanation.walkthrough: Orange blossom is the traditional bridal flower, and Cio-Cio-San in Puccini's opera, known by this nickname, is a bride on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange-tip is an example of the winged insect, and Puccini's bride heroine is Madama of that name.

clue.text: Gear change housing for washers?

parts.note: gear means clothes; a container holding a change of clothes awaiting the washers

explanation.surface: A gearbox casing designed for mechanical washers.
explanation.walkthrough: Gear and washers suggest machinery; gear here is clothing and washers are people doing laundry.
explanation.definitionFit: A wicker hamper holds dirty clothing until it is laundered.

clue.text: Sitting-bower

parts.note: read bower as one who bows: a musician who plays with a bow while seated

explanation.walkthrough: A bower looks like a leafy arbour where one sits; read it as one who bows a stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This string player must sit down to bow the instrument between the knees.

clue.text: Opener backing school theme

parts.note: a key opens a lock

indicators.note: backing in a down clue reads the school's name upwards, backwards

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: A school's first speaker supports its central theme.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is an elite English boarding school.
explanation.definitionFit: A keynote is the central idea or theme of a speech or event.

clue.text: Gas from inert alkalis

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A chemistry note: gas given off by inert alkalis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' is the chemical sense in the surface but means chatter here.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is informal for chatting idly at length.

clue.text: It is standard to carry a brave face

definitions.text: It is standard to carry a brave face

parts.words: It is standard to carry a brave face
parts.note: a carved pole or emblem bearing faces, used as an emblem by a Native American brave's people

explanation.surface: The usual thing is to put on a brave face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave face' reads as courage, but a brave is a Native American warrior whose clan emblem shows carved faces.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved clan emblem acts as a tribal standard and is decorated with faces.

clue.text: 18's pause mark?

definitions.meaning: 18 down is the winged insect; this species has a white mark like the punctuation sign
a punctuation sign indicating a short pause

explanation.walkthrough: '18' refers to 18 down, BUTTERFLY; the comma is a species named for the white mark on its wing.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation sign for a brief pause, and also a species of winged insect named after that sign.

clue.text: Cowshed alongside Royal Exchange

parts.note: by means beside, alongside
E is an abbreviation for exchange

explanation.surface: A cowshed stands beside the Royal Exchange building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Royal Exchange is a historic building in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a farm building for housing cattle.

clue.text: Drink like a fish

definitions.meaning: to drink alcohol habitually and to excess
a small shark of European waters

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as the idiom for heavy drinking, which also defines the answer; the answer is also a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: To tipple heavily is to drink, and the word also names a small shark.

clue.text: Tender, we hear, of dyke builder

indicators.note: we hear says the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to tender is to offer

explanation.surface: Someone bids, it is said, for a dyke builder's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Offa was an 8th-century king of Mercia who built Offa's Dyke along the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: King Offa of Mercia had the great earthwork on the Welsh border constructed.

clue.text: African port raking blunder with oil refining

parts.note: a trip is a stumble or mistake

indicators.note: refining suggests processing crude oil, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: An African port is raking in money despite an oil refining blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Libya's capital is a Mediterranean seaport in North Africa.

clue.text: Why use stairs when leaving pad?

definitions.text: Why use stairs when leaving pad?

parts.words: Why use stairs when leaving pad?
parts.note: a pad is a launch pad; there is an elevator joke in leaving a flat without stairs

explanation.surface: Why walk down the stairs when leaving one's flat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'pad' reads as a home, suggesting taking the elevator; it is a launch pad, which a rocket leaves by rising.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket's launch is the moment it rises from the pad.

clue.text: Decrepit, having provided grub for grub

definitions.meaning: food for a larva: cloth eaten by insect grubs

explanation.walkthrough: Grub is both food and a larva; the clothes moth's larvae eat fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Shabby old fabric has holes chewed by insect larvae, which have fed on it.

clue.text: Taking off table-linen that does not open

indicators.note: does not open means the first letter is missing

parts.note: napery is household linen, especially for the table

explanation.surface: Removing tablecloths that will not unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking off means mimicking, not removing.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking someone off is imitating them, and aping is mimicry.
